title: List Methods
intro: Lists come with **methods** that change them in place: `append` adds one item to the end, `extend` adds several, `insert` puts an item at a position, and `pop` removes and returns one. Assigning a list to a new name doesn't copy it — both names point to the **same** list.

questions.prompt: `pop()` with no index takes the last item; `pop(0)` takes the first. `copy()` makes an independent copy.
questions.exampleCode:
tasks = ["wash"]
tasks.append("cook")
tasks.extend(["shop", "call"])
tasks.insert(0, "wake")
last = tasks.pop()
print(tasks)
print(last)
questions.explanation: `append` adds one item; `extend` adds each item from another list.

questions.prompt: Add `"Cleo"` to the **end** of `queue` and `"Dev"` to the **front**.
questions.hint: `append` for the end, `insert(0, …)` for the front.
questions.explanation: `insert` takes the position first, then the item.

questions.hint: `append` adds exactly one item — even if that item is a list.
questions.explanation: The list `[4, 5]` becomes a single fourth item. `extend` would have added two.

questions.prompt: `orders` holds today's orders. Remove the most recent one (the last) from the list and store it in `latest`.

tests.name: latest
tests.code: assert latest == _original[-1], 'latest should be the last order.'
tests.message: latest should be the last order.

tests.name: shrunk
tests.code: assert orders == _original[:-1], 'The last order should be removed from orders.'
tests.message: orders should no longer contain it.

questions.hint: One method both removes and returns an item.
questions.explanation: `pop()` is perfect for taking the newest item off a list.

questions.prompt: `backup` should keep the playlist as it was **before** the new song, but it changes too. Fix it.

tests.name: playlist
tests.code: assert playlist == ['intro', 'verse', 'chorus'], 'playlist should have the new song.'

questions.hint: `backup = playlist` gives the same list a second name. Make a real copy.

questions.prompt: Fill in the method so `position` is the index of `"c"`.
questions.hint: Which method finds where an item is?
questions.explanation: `index` returns the position of the first match.

questions.prompt: `words` is a list of words. Store how many times `"the"` appears in `count_the`, then remove the **first** `"the"` from the list.

tests.name: count
tests.code: assert count_the == _original.count('the'), 'count_the should be how many times "the" appears.'

tests.name: removed
tests.code:
expected = list(_original)
expected.remove('the')
assert words == expected, 'Remove only the first "the".'

questions.explanation: `remove` works by value; `pop` works by position.
The first item is taken off; the rest shift down.

questions.prompt: A to-do app: move `"buy milk"` from `todo` to the end of `done`, then add `"pay rent"` to the **top** of `todo`.
questions.solution:
todo = ["email Sam", "buy milk", "book dentist"]
done = []
todo.remove("buy milk")
done.append("buy milk")
todo.insert(0, "pay rent")

tests.name: todo
tests.code: assert todo == ['pay rent', 'email Sam', 'book dentist'], 'todo should be ["pay rent", "email Sam", "book dentist"].'

tests.name: done
tests.code: assert done == ['buy milk'], 'done should be ["buy milk"].'

questions.explanation: Each method does one small change; together they move items between lists.
